subject: Founders Surge promo — convertibility and conditional credit proposal
messages:
From: Emma Zhou <emma@foundersurge.vc>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Founders Surge promo - convertibility & conditional credits

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Quick one from our side — Founders Surge is running an 8-week accelerator this fall (cohort starts 9/7) and we want Redwood to be the preferred inference partner. We have a standard promo package for startups (sandbox credits + PR/spotlight) but a few portfolio teams have higher early consumption and have asked whether the promo credits can either:

- a) be issued as a conditional top-up tied to onboarding milestones (so credits vest after integration and first 3 weeks of activity), or
- b) be converted to a short-term dedicated discount (e.g., 20% off dedicated for 3 months) if they plan to move to Reserved/Dedicated early.

Attached is a short MOU and our estimated cohort usage for the three startups that would take the offer. The asks:
- confirmation if conversion to a dedicated discount is possible for promo credits,
- whether we can carve credits by milestone (so unused credits don’t get lost but are only released after production integration), and
- any packaging constraints or billing impacts we should flag to sponsors.

We’re on a tight timeline — would appreciate a quick note of the feasible paths so I can brief the organizers tomorrow.

Thanks,
Emma

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Founders Surge promo - convertibility & conditional credits

Thanks Emma — appreciate the MOU and the usage sketch. Short answer: we can support both paths but there are trade-offs on accounting, invoicing cadence, and SLA scope. High-level options we can offer quickly: 

1) Conditional top-up credits (preferred for sandbox):
   - Credits are held in an escrow-like state and released upon completion of onboarding milestones (we’d define 2 milestones: integration smoke tests, and first-week activity threshold).
   - Unused credits after a 90-day window expire unless both parties agree on extension.
   - No change to SLA or Dedicated guarantees; credits are consumptive on hosted plan.

2) Convertible credits -> Dedicated discount (short-term):
   - We can convert promo credit value into an upfront billing credit against a Dedicated commitment; equivalent value applied as a % discount over N months.
   - Requires a minimum commit (3-month Dedicated reservation) and a simple amendment so procurement/finance can reconcile.
   - Will trigger different invoicing and requires finance sign-off (cc’ing Lauren from Finance).

Can you confirm which cohort teams are likely to pursue Dedicated early vs staying on hosted? If you want, we can draft the amendment language and the milestone checklist. Priyom, can you review the MOU and usage numbers and flag any rollout risks?

— Ben

Ben / Marissa / Emma — I pulled a quick pass on the cohort estimates. Notes below: 

- Usage profile: two teams are likely to spike during demo week (tokens ~2-3M each week for short windows); one is fairly low (sandbox-level).
- Risk: converting credits to Dedicated discount for teams that spike could be cost-effective for them but we need a clear rev-rec/invoice flow to avoid clawbacks.
- Ops ask: if we do conditional top-ups, we should include a single reconciliation checkpoint at 30 days post-release. That keeps ledger clean and reduces ongoing manual audits.

If Founders Surge can share a short sign-off from each startup (simple checkbox + intent to convert), we can auto-provision a draft amendment and the billing stub. Broader point: we should avoid making conditioned credits fully refundable; better to map to future invoice credits.

I’ll draft amendment language after we get signals from Emma on which teams want convertibility.

— Priyom

Thanks Ben / Priyom — quick update from our side. Teams A and B flagged a likely move to Dedicated within 4–6 weeks post-start; Team C will remain hosted. They’ve each filled the intent checkbox in the attached sheet.

Two quick questions:
1) If we convert credits to a dedicated discount and the team doesn’t actually take up Dedicated, can the credit be re-applied to hosted consumption (or is it gone)?
2) For the conditional top-up path, what exact onboarding threshold counts as "first-week activity" — is it a token throughput threshold or an integration ping count?

We’re trying to finalize sponsor communications by EOD Thursday; if you can give us the short answers + a one-paragraph amendment template, that’d be ideal.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Re: Request: Founders Surge promo - convertibility & conditional credits

Emma — thanks for the quick clarification. Short answers inline: 

1) Convertibility fallback: If a team signs the intent and we convert credit value into a Dedicated billing credit but they never take Dedicated within 90 days, the remaining credit value can be re-applied to hosted consumption once finance confirms (subject to a small reconciliation fee to cover invoice adjustments). We’ll capture that in the amendment.

2) Onboarding threshold: we’ll use a two-part signal — (a) a successful onboarding smoke test (API keys and KV cache warm) plus (b) a minimum of 12 successful inference calls within the first 7 calendar days. That’s measurable and avoids token-based gaming. If teams expect bursty demo-week traffic, we can add a one-off demo waiver for the demo week spike.

Action items: 
- Priyom will prepare a one-paragraph amendment template and a milestone checklist (ETA: EOD Wed).
- Lauren (Finance) will prepare a billing stub for converting credit value into a Dedicated discount and outline the invoice flow (ETA: EOD Thu).
- Emma to confirm which teams want convertibility (by Thu EOD).

We’ll draft the amendment and circulate for signatures once we have the confirmations. Happy to hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk through examples.

— Ben
